title: PPC: critical-width partial-pivot collimation with a square-root base

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, PPC is the single critical-profile, square-root-base algorithm specified in proof.md Sections 1-7, with n=ceil(log2 N), L=log2 n. For n>=256 it uses the least sequentially feasible maximum width B, decrement ceil(log2((q(b)+2)^2)), q(b)=b+ceil(log2(b+1))+4, and base U=ceil(sqrt(B)); it is not the separate quarter-base comparison configuration. For 1<=n<256 it uses the specified exhaustive branch. From independent ideal source copies it returns the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3. Total charged sequential work is O(n^(11/4) L^(13/4) 2^((177/250)sqrt(nL))). For n>=256, the stronger exact-profile bound is O(n B^(7/2) log2(B+2)^(-1/2) log2(n+2)^2 2^(B/2)). It includes classical bit operations, addressing, circuit generation, every acquisition, extraction precision, decoding, retries and abort work. The supported envelope has exact growth index 1/2. All four bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, including wrong labels, incorrect earlier estimates, failures and aborts. The asymptotic representatives apply for n>=2; every 1<=n<256, including n=1, uses the specified finite branch. Constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes.

For n>=256, the stronger profile cap is O(n B^(3/2) 2^((B-U)/2)). The supported envelope has exact growth index 1/2. For every integer N>=2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, PPC is the single critical-profile, square-root-base algorithm specified in proof.md Sections 1-7, with n=ceil(log2 N), L=log2 n. For n>=256 it uses the least sequentially feasible maximum width B, decrement ceil(log2((q(b)+2)^2)), q(b)=b+ceil(log2(b+1))+4, and base U=ceil(sqrt(B)); it is not the separate quarter-base comparison configuration. For 1<=n<256 it uses the specified exhaustive branch. From independent ideal source copies it returns the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3. For every n>=1 the guaranteed malformed fraction is epsilon(n)=0: at most floor(0*Q)=0 acquisitions may be malformed, so every acquired copy is an independent ideal coset state. Under exactly this model, the same unconditional success and all four every-branch resource bounds hold jointly. No positive tolerance or impossibility of positive tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
